reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address CrFeCoNiAl alloys or the formation of protective α-Al2O3 in this system. E1 discusses Sn-rich layers and oxygen contamination in Nb-Si alloys, while E2 describes failure to form α-Al2O3 in a different Nb-Ti-Si-Al-Hf system, providing no support for the key premises about Al-driven selective oxidation in CrFeCoNiAl.
premises: Selective oxidation of Al can form a continuous α-Al2O3 scale in CrFeCoNiAl alloys above 900°C
α-Al2O3 scale minimizes oxygen ion diffusion and interfacial stresses, preventing cracking/spallation
Optimal Al concentration suppresses competing, less protective oxides from other alloying elements
Crystallographic compatibility of α-Al2O3 with the underlying alloy minimizes interfacial stress
